If your goal is to hit back while still sounding credible, I'd avoid personal insults like "degenerate" because they tend to distract from your strongest points. Here's a version that's cutting, but stays focused on the facts.

:::writing{variant="chat_message" id="58732"}
As I said before, I'm actively working on getting this resolved, and I'll continue to keep you updated.

As for your suggestions, I don't rely on my parents or ask my boyfriend to take on my financial obligations. I handle my own responsibilities. I'm also not going to involve people who had nothing to do with this lease in the first place.

The reality is that this situation exists because the lease was structured upside down with no money down. I'm doing everything I can to fix it, even though I didn't create it.

Once I have another option, I'll let you know. Until then, I'm continuing to work on a solution.
:::

This version puts the responsibility back where you believe it belongs without giving him obvious inflammatory statements he could use to escalate the conversation.

If your goal is to be direct and set the record straight without giving him unnecessary ammunition, I'd keep it sharp and factual rather than insulting.

:::writing{variant="chat_message" id="42618"}
I am working on getting this resolved, and I'll continue to keep you updated.

As for the rest, I don't rely on other people to solve my financial obligations. I'm not going to ask my parents or my boyfriend to co-sign my debt. That's not how I handle my finances.

Ironically, this situation exists because the original lease was structured upside down with no money down. I'm exploring every legitimate option to correct it, but I'm not going to involve people who have nothing to do with it.

I'll let you know as soon as I have a solution.
:::

Here's a concise, professional response you can send.

:::writing{variant="email" id="73841" subject="Car Loan Update"}
Hi,

I've been looking into every option I can find to get your name off the car, but so far I haven't had any luck.

At this point, the dealership has told me the only option they've offered is to sell the car back to them, and they would require approximately $5,000 to complete the transaction.

I'm still looking for other possible solutions, and if I find one, I'll let you know. I wanted to keep you updated on where things currently stand.

Thanks,
Bethany
:::

If you'd like, I can also make it a little firmer or more collaborative, depending on the tone you want to set.

Please respond to my ex-husband that I am not a fucking degenerate adult. Who relies on mommy and daddy to pay for my own bills. Nor would I ask an individual who has nothing to do with my finances to cosign on an event because I'm not a degenerator. I don't make enough money to be on the lease myself. He's the one that got me into this fucking dumbass upside down lease because he was too cheap to put any money down and he is in irresponsible with finances. Respond short and sweet, but to the point cutthroat and remember that he's a complete narcissistic piece of shit who relies on mommy's money 24/7 to float his way through life and I wouldn't never do that

Why can't your boyfriend cosign with you. I signed for your Acura when we were in California, and we had only been together for a few months. You guys have been together longer than when I co-signed with you. Not trying to get in your business but that doesn't make any sense that you can't find someone if not him even your parents to co-sign with you.
I do want to work with you if that is possible, but you will have to start making the payments if you cannot figure this out. I don't want you to be without a vehicle, but you cannot be late with the payments moving forward.
